paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: Jesus wants your heart in the right place, and your treasure is what shows where that is. He says, "For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also." (Matthew 6:21) Treasure on earth gets eaten by moth and rust or carried off by thieves, but treasure in heaven stays safe. Then He puts it plainly: "You cannot serve both God and money." (Matthew 6:24)

Now, here's why the worry part sits right next to the treasure part. Worry is what happens when we try to hold up our own tomorrow with our own two hands. I did that for years in the back of a junk drawer, and I'm telling you, it paid NOTHING. Jesus points to the birds and says, "your heavenly Father feeds them," and then asks, "Are you not much more valuable than they?" (Matthew 6:26)

So where does that leave you? Jesus doesn't just say stop worrying. He gives you something to do instead: "seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness, and all these things will be added unto you." (Matthew 6:33) Your Father already knows what you need (Matthew 6:32), so you can put God first and hand Him the rest. And when tomorrow shows up with its own troubles, you can meet it then, because "Today has enough trouble of its own." (Matthew 6:34) The story isn't over, friend, because Jesus is still teaching up on that mountain.
